Definition: from G4253 and G3958; to undergo hardship previously:--suffer before.
BiblicalUsage: Propascho means to suffer before, to have undergone hardship previously. Paul uses it once, reminding the Thessalonians that after we had suffered before and were shamefully entreated at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe suffering before is the doorway to boldness after, and the shame at Philippi became the boldness at Thessalonica.
